title: U.S. House · Ohio's 14th District
area: Northeast Ohio, including Lake, Geauga and Ashtabula counties and part of eastern Cuyahoga County.

context.text: Incumbent David Joyce (R) defeated Nicole Frenchko in the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Maria Jukic (D) defeated Bill O'Neill and Carl Setzer in the Democratic primary.

summary.text: David Joyce is the Republican incumbent in Ohio's 14th Congressional District, which he has represented since January 2013. A lawyer, he worked as a public defender and served as Geauga County Prosecutor for nearly 25 years before entering Congress. He serves on the House Appropriations Committee, where he chairs the Financial Services and General Government Subcommittee.

background.text: Born March 17, 1957, in Cleveland, Ohio, according to Wikipedia; his official biography describes him as a lifelong Ohioan who was born and raised in Northeast Ohio.

Earned a Bachelor of Science in accounting from the University of Dayton in 1979 and later a Juris Doctor from the University of Dayton, according to Wikipedia; his official biography confirms the Dayton law degree.
Worked as a public defender, according to his official biography; Wikipedia dates this work to Cuyahoga County (1983-84) and Geauga County (1985-88).

Elected Geauga County Prosecutor in 1988 and served in that role for nearly 25 years, according to his official biography. Wikipedia reports that his office prosecuted the 2012 Chardon High School shooting case.

Became the Republican nominee for the 14th District in 2012 after Rep. Steve LaTourette announced his retirement following the primary and local party leaders selected Joyce as the replacement nominee (per Wikipedia); he won the November 2012 general election.
Won re-election in 2022 (61.7% over Democrat Matt Kilboy) and 2024 (63.4% over Democrat Brian Kenderes), and the May 5, 2026 Republican primary (70.3% over Nicole Frenchko).
Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, including its Defense Subcommittee, and chairs its Financial Services and General Government Subcommittee in the 119th Congress.

Chaired the Republican Governance Group during the 118th Congress, co-founded the Bipartisan Task Force to End Sexual Violence in the 115th Congress, and is Vice Chair of the Addiction, Treatment and Recovery Caucus, according to his official biography.
According to his official biography, he lives in Bainbridge Township, Ohio, with his wife, Kelly; they have three children.

record.text: Chairs the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Financial Services and General Government (119th Congress, 2025-2026), also sitting on the Defense subcommittee.
Served as ranking member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies and on the House Committee on Ethics in the 117th Congress (2021-2022).

summary.text: Maria Jukic is the Democratic nominee in Ohio's 14th Congressional District. An attorney and former Euclid city councilwoman, she spent more than two decades in healthcare communications and arts programs at Euclid Hospital and the Cleveland Clinic. She describes her campaign as an effort to listen and find common ground.

background.text: Born in Cleveland to a Croatian-American working-class family; in her survey response she says her mother was in the UAW and her father was a draftsman.
Graduated from Villa Angela Academy, where she says she was class president and valedictorian.

Earned a bachelor's degree in American Studies from the University of Notre Dame, a master's in theology and religious studies from John Carroll University, and a law degree from Cleveland State University College of Law; she also describes holding a Fulbright Fellowship.

Describes 24 years in healthcare, in marketing and public affairs at Euclid Hospital and in arts and medicine at the Cleveland Clinic; the Tribune Chronicle identified her in 2024 as senior director of arts and medicine in the Cleveland Clinic's Office of Patient Experience.
Elected to Euclid City Council as a Democrat in November 2019, served a four-year term, and did not seek re-election in 2023.
Filed in March 2024 to run for the 14th District seat as an independent candidate.
Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 50.7% of the vote, ahead of Bill O'Neill and Carl Setzer, and is a licensed attorney.

sources.title: Joyce cruises in congressional primary; Jukic wins Democratic vote

researchNotes: Neither Maria Jukic's nor David Joyce's campaign website was reviewed. Joyce has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey and Ballotpedia's biography section for him contains no independent text beyond his committee record, so his biography relies on his official house.gov page and Wikipedia. Jukic completed the survey, but her priorities and positions have not yet been added to this guide. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals for Joyce are added separately.
